questions.stem: What does the proverb 'A stitch in time saves nine' mean?

options.option_text: Tailors who work quickly earn more (literal/incorrect interpretation)
Dealing with a problem promptly prevents it from worsening (correct: taking early action saves much more work later ✓)
Nine stitches are always better than one (misses the point entirely)
Time spent sewing is always worthwhile (irrelevant to the proverb's meaning)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'A stitch in time saves nine' means that a timely action now prevents greater effort later. Fixing a small hole (one stitch) early stops it from becoming a large tear (nine stitches). Moral: act on problems early before they become bigger.

questions.stem: What does 'Actions speak louder than words' mean?

options.option_text: Shouting is more effective than writing (literal misreading)
What a person does is more important than what they say (correct: actions reveal character better than promises ✓)
Physical strength is more important than communication skills (not the proverb's meaning)
Quiet people are generally more trustworthy (opposite reading)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Actions speak louder than words' = what you DO matters more than what you SAY. People may promise things but their real character is revealed by their actions. 'He says he cares but never helps — actions speak louder than words.'

questions.stem: 'All that glitters is not gold' means:

options.option_text: Gold always has a bright shine (literal and irrelevant to figurative meaning)
Things that appear valuable or attractive may not actually be so (correct: appearances can be deceptive ✓)
Only gold is worth investing in (misses the figurative meaning)
Precious metals should be tested before purchase (too literal)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'All that glitters is not gold' = things that look attractive or valuable on the surface may not be genuinely good. Don't judge by appearances. Origin: Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice. 'She was dazzled by his charm, but all that glitters is not gold.'

questions.stem: Choose the correct meaning of 'Birds of a feather flock together':

options.option_text: Birds of the same species always stay together in flocks (literal — not the figurative meaning)
People with similar tastes, interests, or characters tend to associate with each other (correct ✓)
Feathers are important for bird identification (completely wrong context)
One should avoid keeping company with troublesome people (related idea, but not the proverb's direct meaning)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Birds of a feather flock together' = people with similar interests, values, or character naturally come together. 'He and his friends are always in trouble — birds of a feather flock together.' It's an observation about human social behaviour, not a moral judgment.

questions.stem: 'Don't count your chickens before they are hatched' advises:

options.option_text: Always count your animals regularly (literal farm advice)
Don't make plans based on something that hasn't happened yet (correct: don't assume success prematurely ✓)
Chickens should never be counted in advance (too literal)
One should be cautious while rearing poultry (irrelevant)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Don't count your chickens before they are hatched' = don't assume something will succeed and plan around it before it has actually happened. 'He spent the prize money before the competition ended — he was counting his chickens before they were hatched.'

questions.stem: What does 'The pen is mightier than the sword' mean?

options.option_text: Writing implements are physically stronger than weapons (literal/absurd)
Written words and ideas have more lasting influence than military force (correct: the power of writing exceeds that of violence ✓)
Educated people always defeat soldiers in battle (misinterpretation)
Swords are obsolete weapons in modern times (not the proverb's meaning)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'The pen is mightier than the sword' = communication, writing, and ideas have more lasting power than brute force or violence. Coined by Edward Bulwer-Lytton in 1839. 'Mahatma Gandhi's writings moved millions — the pen is indeed mightier than the sword.'

questions.stem: 'Every cloud has a silver lining' means:

options.option_text: Clouds contain moisture which reflects sunlight (meteorological fact, not proverb meaning)
Every difficult or unpleasant situation has some positive aspect (correct: there is hope in every bad situation ✓)
Rainy weather always leads to sunny days (too literal)
Silver is found in cloud formations (scientifically wrong and misses the point)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Every cloud has a silver lining' = even in the worst situations, there is always something positive or hopeful. 'She lost her job but found a better one — every cloud has a silver lining.' The 'silver lining' = the bright edge visible around a cloud blocking the sun.

questions.stem: Choose the correct meaning of 'Barking dogs seldom bite':

options.option_text: Dogs that bark are usually aggressive (literal, opposite of the proverb's meaning)
People who make the most threats or noise are seldom the most dangerous (correct: those who threaten loudly rarely follow through ✓)
Silent dogs are more dangerous than noisy ones (related but not the standard phrasing)
Animals that growl should always be feared (opposite of the proverb)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Barking dogs seldom bite' = people who talk loudly or make the most threats usually don't act on them. The most dangerous people are often the quietest. 'Don't worry about his threats — barking dogs seldom bite.'

questions.stem: What does 'Strike while the iron is hot' mean?

options.option_text: Blacksmiths must work quickly when metal is heated (literal/craft advice only)
Take advantage of an opportunity while conditions are favourable (correct: act at the right moment ✓)
Anger should be expressed immediately (misapplication — 'hot' doesn't refer to emotion here)
Iron tools should be used quickly before they cool down (too literal)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Strike while the iron is hot' = act at the best time; take advantage of a favourable opportunity before it passes. From blacksmithing — iron must be shaped while it's hot and malleable. 'He got a job offer and accepted immediately — strike while the iron is hot.'

questions.stem: 'Too many cooks spoil the broth' means:

options.option_text: Large kitchens need many cooks to produce good food (opposite of the proverb)
When too many people are involved in a task, it is likely to go wrong (correct: too many decision-makers causes confusion ✓)
Cooking is best left to professionals (unrelated interpretation)
Soup should only be cooked by one person at a time (too literal)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Too many cooks spoil the broth' = when too many people are involved in making decisions or doing a task, the result is often worse because everyone interferes. 'The project failed because everyone had opinions but no single leader — too many cooks spoil the broth.'
